ASSURANCE / INDEPENDENT TOPIC

Who can take part?

The second worked example: selected markup evidence, human evaluation and accessible journeys in use.

The current assessment covers five homepage entry routes. Levels describe evidence maturity within that scope; every topic keeps its own requirements and open work.

Accessibility

Level 2 — Mechanically checked

Selected homepage markup checks across five entry routes. Human keyboard, assistive-technology, reflow and visual evaluation remain open.

  • Scope of accessibility evaluation · supported · level 1 — Authored scope and explicit boundaries.
  • Document language markers · supported · level 2 — Current generated entry markup; presence checks only.
  • Skip-link target · supported · level 2 — Current generated entry markup; presence checks only.
  • Image alternative attributes · supported · level 2 — Current generated entry markup; presence checks only.
  • Human accessibility evaluation · not-evidenced · level 3 — Evaluate keyboard and focus journeys, screen-reader use, zoom/reflow and visual contrast; record findings and coverage.
  • Journeys with disabled participants · not-evidenced · level 4 — Observe representative tasks with people with disabilities and record barriers and resolution.
  • Accessibility maintenance · not-evidenced · level 5 — Assign ownership, review cadence and regression evidence for the assessed journeys.

See the evidence roadmap →

What the current evidence establishes

The automatic checks cover document language markers, a skip link with its target and image alt-attribute presence. Alternative-text meaning, focus order, keyboard operation, assistive technology, reflow and visual contrast remain evaluation work. WCAG conformance requires a separate scoped evaluation.
